title: Lucky No. 13: Giants’ Odell Beckham Jr. to wear number he made famous in New York
content:
Get nostalgic, Giants fans. Not only is Odell Beckham Jr. back in a New York Giants uniform, but the franchise icon is now wearing No. 13, the jersey number he made famous in New York a decade ago.

The team made the announcement on its social media accounts Tuesday morning.

Beckham has been wearing No. 3 throughout the preseason. Fellow wide receiver Jalin Hyatt had been wearing No. 13, but Hyatt did not make the Giants’ 53-man roster, though he did sign with the Giants’ practice squad.

“I think we all know what that (number) means to me,” Beckham said Monday after he’d been told he made the roster but had yet to officially reclaim his old number. “It would be an honor and a privilege to put that back on.”

The number doesn’t just mean a lot to Beckham and Giants fans. NFL fans around the world once made Beckham’s No. 13 Giants jersey one of the most popular in football. Following a sensational rookie campaign in 2014, in which Beckham recorded 91 receptions for 1,305 yards and 12 touchdowns and won NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, his jersey led all non-quarterback jersey sales on the official NFL online shop, according to an ESPN report. In 2016, Dick’s Sporting Goods reported that Beckham’s jersey was their most sold jersey entering the 2016 season.

For Beckman, while it will be a thrill to wear his old jersey number again, the bigger thrill will be wearing a Giants jersey in a regular-season game again.

“Man, it means everything to me,” Beckham said of making the team.

Beckham learned that he’d made the team after the Giants’ final preseason game on Friday and said that became emotional.

“Just my family, being here, seeing my son at the game. … I had those tears when I got back to the hotel after figuring out I’m going to be here,” Beckham said Monday. “And I have an opportunity to re-write some of the last bit of the chapter. Don’t know last year, whatever it is, I just know I’m going to give my all. But definitely had that moment where it was like you could let out some of the pain that I went through. It was a very healing, very emotional. Something I was very happy about.”

It’s been a long journey back to New York for Beckham, who was traded to the Cleveland Browns following the 2018 season. The two-time All-Pro spent parts of three seasons in Cleveland before joining the Los Angeles Rams for their Super Bowl run in 2021. He tore his ACL in the Rams’ win that night and missed the entire 2022 season. After that, he signed on with Harbaugh’s Baltimore Ravens in 2023, catching 35 passes for 565 yards and three touchdowns. He then played nine games for the Miami Dolphins in 2024 but remained unsigned last season as he served a six-game suspension for violating the NFL’s policy on performance-enhancing drugs.

“The last two years I talked to y’all about just the spiritual journey that I’ve been on,” Beckham said Monday. “The growth, the humility. Kind of walking through life over the last two years — a bit of hardships, with myself feeling, just wasn’t where I wanted to be. And now being able to be here, to walk in here, I remember coming here to practice and seeing the ‘86, the ‘90, the 2007 (and) ‘11 (championship) banners. And I was like, ‘Man, I just want to bring one here.’”
